summary: Drawer — the bottom panel dismissed by dragging it down, and a SECOND overlay alongside Sheet rather than a variant of it. The distinction is the gesture, not the geometry: a Sheet is anchored to a side edge and closes on scrim or Escape; a Drawer carries a handle, follows the finger, and closes past a distance or a velocity. Adding side="bottom" to a Sheet would ship a drawer that cannot be dragged, which is the worst of both, so CONVENTIONS gains a §7a overlay taxonomy table (Popover / Modal / Sheet / Drawer) keyed on how each is dismissed and where it comes from — written after this pair was briefly collapsed into one component by mistake. Base UI supplies the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and focus restoration (ADR 0012); the drag is ours, with no drag library entering the dependency list. Open state is held by the component rather than left to Base UI, because the handle has to close a drawer nobody is controlling from outside. Two decisions worth their own line. The handle is a real BUTTON as well as a drag target: WCAG 2.5.7 requires a single-pointer alternative to any dragging movement, and the honest one is the same control responding to a tap — not a second control hidden elsewhere. And it spans the full 32px band the sheet draws rather than the 8px bar inside it, because the bar alone would be an 8px target against SC 2.5.8's 24px floor. The velocity threshold measures the LAST segment of the gesture rather than averaging the whole of it — averaging punishes the common shape (grab, pause to read, then decide) by reporting a slow flick, and rewards a fast grab followed by a long hold with a flick it never made; the bug surfaced as a leisurely 40px test drag dismissing the drawer, because synthetically-dispatched events land within a millisecond of each other and made every drag read as infinitely fast. Design defects corrected in Paper: the scrim was --ui-bg-emphasis-active, an opaque surface role with no alpha, where --ui-scrim is the role that exists for exactly this; the panel used --ui-nav-bg and --ui-nav-border on a surface holding a form rather than navigation; the primary action was a raw --ui-blue-80; and the handle's radius was a literal calc(infinity * 1px) beside a --ui-radius-full on its sibling.
